- Taro, the 3D question: a three.js sketch from primitives looked like a toy. Rendered a Blender

- Added a read-only Supabase MCP for the generator's project (local config); it needs sign-in.
  It can read the database but can't download storage files.
- New session, from the handover. Committed the Taro script and sketches (`4f850ce`). The
  Taro Blender loop over the map is at https://claude.ai/artifact/92cvEod15QB1Mm5MMZXmL6 and
  the rejected three.js sketch at https://claude.ai/artifact/9JiZ8LTLfc5jkBNFYwDcmG.
- Supabase MCP signed in and working. **Taro has no three-view portraits.** `style_cast` has
  "Taro the kitten" and "Taro the cat", both with `portrait_id` null. Each has one `style_refs`
  image, 1264×848 JPEG, in the private `style-refs` bucket (`b5f76d95-…/80f51fd1-…` kitten,
  `b5f76d95-…/e5115d54-…` cat). A single landscape image is probably a turnaround sheet, so
  Tripo Multiview would need it cropped into views, or `tripo_h3_1_image_to_3d` from one view.
  The MCP can't download it; Yan has to save it, or the generator's MCP gets a download tool.
- Surveyed the SvelteKit repos in `~/Coding_work`. The usual setup is npm, adapter-vercel,
  Tailwind v4 via `@tailwindcss/vite`, TypeScript and Svelte 5 runes. The newest variant is the
  generator's (kit config inside `vite.config.ts`, forced runes, vite 8, TS 6, ESLint 10,
  Prettier with tabs, vitest). Scaffolded this repo to match it: the same devDependency
  versions and the same config files, without the generator's app dependencies. The design
  tokens are in `src/routes/layout.css` `@theme`, and everything is prerendered. `check`, `lint`
  and `build` pass. A placeholder page sits at `/`. No Playwright yet: there's nothing to test
  end to end until Taro and the map are in.
- **Taro reference views.** Yan generated four separate views (front, left, back, right) of
  both Taro the kitten and Taro the cat from a generator session, using a prompt written here.
  They're 2138² and 2092² PNGs on white, in `art/taro/refs/`, next to the original sheets.
  Picked the **kitten**: short, round limbs and a short tail rebuild far better in image-to-3D
  than the adult's thin legs and long tail, and "under construction" suits a kitten that's
  still growing. The kitten views match: equal height on the same baseline, the tail seen
  end-on from the back, no whiskers or shading baked in.
- **Taro mesh.** Higgsfield `tripo_h3_1_multiview_to_3d` with detailed geometry and texture,
  18 credits (Yan approved; quad output would have cost 19.5). Job
  `78db19f3-b7c2-473e-8c85-bc5280fcfdee`. The result is
  `art/taro/model/taro-kitten-tripo.glb`, 62 MB and gitignored (re-download from the job if
  needed). Inspected in Blender: one mesh, all four legs separate, the tail free of the body,
  ears clean, 4096² colour, normal and ORM maps (matte, non-metallic). The model faces +X. It
  is **1.9M triangles**, far too dense to rig; it needs decimating or remeshing to roughly
  20–50k before the Rigify cat metarig.
- **Taro rig** ([plan](../plans/2026-10-04_taro-rig-and-clips.plan.md)). `art/taro/taro_rig.py`
  rebuilds `taro-kitten.blend` from the GLB in about 1.5 minutes. Steps:
  - Weld the glTF's UV-seam splits. Without this the ink pass drew lines across the body, and
    the seams would tear when bent.
  - Decimate to 40k triangles and turn Taro to face −Y. `rotation_euler` doesn't work on
    glTF imports, which use quaternions, so the script rotates the mesh data instead.
  - Apply the toon material with the painted texture.
  - Build a 30-bone skeleton using Rigify cat names. The metarig's 100-odd face bones are
    pointless on a painted face.
  - Weight with bone heat, then confine the ear weights: bone heat gave each ear about
    1,550 vertices of skull.

  The deformation sheet (head turn, head tilt, tail swing, ear flick, paw lift) is clean.
- Yan on the rigged Taro in Blender: "looks fantastic". So the comic look (toon shading and
  ink) stays.
- **Taro clips.** `art/taro/taro_clips.py` renders `idle`, `ear-flick`, `tail-swish` and
  `look-up`. Each is a full 96-frame idle cycle with one moment layered on, so every clip starts
  and ends on idle's first frame and the site can cut between them at loop boundaries.
  - Checked: every clip's first frame is identical to idle's frame 1, and the loop seam
    (frame 96 back to frame 1) is the size of a normal frame step (0.72 against 0.68–0.81).
  - `art/taro/encode.sh` makes WebM files of 134–158 KB (alpha confirmed) and HEVC `.mp4`
    files of about 1.07 MB.
  - Preview with a random clip mixer over the map:
    https://claude.ai/artifact/Trw9tAciyJn1qZtWVHysAg
  - Rendering takes about 7–10 s a frame, mostly Freestyle. Four Blender processes at once was
    too much for this machine (Yan), so two at a time.
  - Two of those processes hung at startup in the user add-on BlenderGIS; render with
    `--factory-startup`.
  - ffmpeg decodes the HEVC alpha as opaque, which proves nothing. Safari and the iPhone are
    the real check.
- Yan's changes to the preview: Taro **says** the line in a speech bubble with a short tail
  pointing at the head, and the map is a very faint wash (12%).
- **Holding page built and deployed.**
  - `src/lib/taro/clips.ts` has the mixer's choices (next clip, video format) as pure
    functions, with 12 unit tests written first.
  - `TaroMixer.svelte` only plays the videos. The page has the faint map, the bubble, the footer
    band, meta tags and a share card.
  - Favicon: the glass-sphere watershed from panel PAO:5:1, put in by Yan and a generator
    session.
  - CI is GitHub Actions (check, lint, test, build). CD is Vercel's Git integration on the new
    project `riverbanks-microsite` in `yanthibicos-projects`.
  - Live at https://riverbanks-microsite.vercel.app. `riverbanks.lol` is not attached yet.
- **Bug, fixed:** on the first deploy Yan saw that Taro didn't animate. The mixer started from an
  `$effect` on the video format, which ran before `bind:this` had handed over the `<video>`
  elements, so nothing ever played. It now starts from the idle video's own `canplay` (`6b12d07`).
  Headless Chrome kept hanging on screenshots; `--dump-dom` and grepping the deployed JS were the
  checks that worked.
- **Safari wouldn't play Taro, desktop or iPhone.** `#debug` showed "Media failed to decode"
  on every `.mp4`. Two separate faults:
  - ffmpeg's `hevc_videotoolbox` makes HEVC-with-alpha files that Apple's decoder can't read
    (on this Intel Mac).
  - Remuxing a good `.mov` to `.mp4` with ffmpeg breaks it too.

  `encode.sh` now goes PNG → ProRes 4444 → `avconvert` (preset
  `PresetHEVCHighestQualityWithAlpha`), writing the `.mp4` directly. That gives 0.9–0.96 MB
  files that decode with 73% transparency. Each file is checked with AVFoundation
  (`art/taro/check-alpha.swift`), which reproduces Safari's failure, so a bad encode now stops
  there. The earlier "-11801/-12713, probably the sandbox" reading was wrong: that error was the
  bug.

  Also fixed on the way: iOS loads no video data before `play()`, so `canplay` never fired.
  Videos now register through `{@attach}` and idle plays at once (`00981a6`).
- Yan confirmed Taro animates in desktop Safari and on an iPhone. On the iPhone, `#debug` first
  showed `NotAllowedError`: Low Power Mode (yellow battery) blocks all autoplay. Added a fallback
  (`f7de93c`): the first tap starts Taro and unlocks all four clips. Not yet tested with Low Power
  Mode on. An animated WebP for that case is possible, but larger; not done.
